_meta.description: Universal OAuth/account-chooser handler for Yeshie. Detects OAuth surface type (same-page nav, iframe, separate window) and coordinates multi-window account selection and consent flows.
_meta.author: Yeshie architecture research

oauth_email.description: Email to select in account chooser (Google, Microsoft, etc.)

oauth_app_name.description: App name for consent screen (e.g., 'gmail-bridge' for 'Sign in to gmail-bridge')

parent_tab_id.description: MCP-tagged tab ID of initiating app (if known). Used to route window.open() popups back to tab registry.

base_url.description: Base URL of OAuth initiation site (fallback navigation if needed)

timeout_ms.description: Max time to wait for account selection and consent completion

notes: This is a PROTOTYPE — not yet tested against real OAuth flows.
Three OAuth surface types are documented but only window.open() case (surface 3) is architecturally problematic.
Surface 1 & 2 (same-page nav, iframe): current Yeshie can already handle via content-script injection.
Surface 3 (window.open popup in different Chrome window): requires extension to adopt popup via chrome.tabs.query + new MCP tool.
See DESIGN NOTES section below for detailed surface analysis and what extension changes are needed.

chain.note: Pre-chain: verify we're on an OAuth initiation page (SSO button visible or consent flow starting).
Detect OAuth surface type. Initially: same-page nav (account chooser appears in current page). Set window.__yeshieOAuthSurface = 'same_page_nav' | 'iframe' | 'window_open'.
If surface = same-page nav: account chooser appears below SSO button. Jump to account selection.
If surface = iframe: OAuth provider redirects into an iframe. Same selection logic applies, but content script must find selector within iframe.
If surface = window.open: OAuth redirects to separate Chrome window outside MCP tab group. Requires popup adoption via chrome.tabs.query.

target.name: account_chooser_option
target.description: Account option matching oauth_email in chooser (data-email, data-identifier, or text match)

chain.note: Click the account matching oauth_email. Expected response: navigation to consent screen (URL contains 'consent', 'permissions', or 'authorize').

chain.code: ({msg: 'WINDOW_OPEN_DETECTED: Use chrome.tabs.query + MCP tool to find and focus popup tab. See DESIGN NOTES.'})
chain.note: ESCALATION POINT: If window.open() popup detected (separate Chrome window), extension cannot reach it via content script. Requires new MCP tool: yeshie_query_tabs() + yeshie_adopt_popup(popup_tab_id).

target.name: consent_screen_button
target.description: Consent button on OAuth provider consent screen ('Continue', 'Allow', 'Authorize')

chain.note: Wait for consent screen to load. Button text varies: 'Continue', 'Allow', 'Authorize', 'Grant access'.
Click consent button. Fallback text patterns: 'Allow', 'Authorize', 'Grant', 'Approve'.
Wait for final redirect back to the application. URL should no longer be on the OAuth provider domain.
Verify OAuth flow completed: popup closed, parent tab shows authenticated state (nav drawer present, session cookie set).

stateGraph.notes: Three-state model: before OAuth, during account selection, after consent.

oauth_initiating.description: On SSO button or OAuth initiation page

signals.selector: button:has-text('Sign in with Google'), button:has-text('Sign in with Microsoft'), [role='button']:has-text('Continue with')

account_chooser_same_page.description: Account chooser inline on current page (no navigation or iframe)

account_chooser_iframe.description: Account chooser inside an iframe on current page

popup_opened_separate_window.description: OAuth opened a separate browser window (window.open). Current tab is waiting for popup to complete.

oauth_complete.description: OAuth flow finished, back to app with valid session

DESIGN_NOTES.title: Yeshie OAuth Architecture Analysis
DESIGN_NOTES.summary: Three OAuth surface types exist. Yeshie currently handles surfaces 1 & 2. Surface 3 (window.open popup) breaks because the popup lands in a separate Chrome window outside our MCP tab group.

surfaces.name: Same-page navigation
surfaces.description: OAuth provider redirects in the same tab. Account chooser and consent screens appear inline or in a modal overlay.
surfaces.example: Clicking 'Sign in with Google' navigates to accounts.google.com in the current tab. Chooser appears as a list item list. No new windows.
surfaces.reason: Content script is already injected. Can query selectors, click, wait for redirects.

surfaces.name: OAuth in iframe
surfaces.description: OAuth provider content (chooser, consent) is embedded in an <iframe> on the current page.
surfaces.example: Current tab shows an iframe with src='https://accounts.google.com/...'. Chooser and consent live inside the iframe.
surfaces.reason: Content script can detect iframe presence and wait for redirect out. But querying/clicking inside iframe requires cross-origin iframe access, which may be blocked by X-Frame-Options.
surfaces.breaking_case: If iframe is cross-origin and doesn't allow CDP/extension access, content script cannot reach selectors inside. Workaround: wait for iframe to redirect the parent tab (most OAuth flows eventually pop out of iframe).

surfaces.name: Separate Chrome window (window.open)
surfaces.description: OAuth provider opens a new popup window via window.open() or Chrome's native popup mechanism. Account chooser and consent appear in this new window, which may be in a different Chrome tab group.
surfaces.example: Apps Script 'Review permissions' opens a popup for 'Sign in to gmail-bridge'. The popup is a full Chrome window, not in our MCP tab group.
surfaces.reason: Content script cannot reach a window that is outside the MCP tab group. chrome.tabs.query can find it, but only the background worker has access to chrome.tabs. No MCP tool currently exposes cross-window tab queries or popup adoption.
surfaces.breaking_case: Apps Script oauth flow, Google Drive permission requests, any OAuth using native Chrome popup. THIS IS THE IMMEDIATE BLOCKER.

minimum_extension_work.title: What's blocking surface 3 (popup window)?
minimum_extension_work.problem: When OAuth opens window.open(), the popup tab is outside our MCP-tagged tab group. Content script can't reach it. Background worker can query it with chrome.tabs.query, but there's no MCP tool to ask the background worker for this info.

solution_steps.title: Add MCP tool: yeshie_query_tabs()
solution_steps.description: Background worker exposes a new MCP tool that returns all open tabs matching a pattern (URL, windowId, title). Caller can find popups.
solution_steps.pseudocode: yeshie_query_tabs({ urlPattern: 'accounts.google.com', windowId: <any>, title: <any> }) → [{tabId, url, title, windowId}, ...]
solution_steps.location: ~/Projects/cc-bridge-mcp/server.js (add MCP tool that calls background worker's chrome.tabs.query)

solution_steps.title: Add socket.io listener: query_tabs
solution_steps.description: Background worker listens for socket.io 'query_tabs' message from relay, responds with filtered tab list.

solution_steps.title: Add step action: focus_tab
solution_steps.description: New payload action to focus/activate a specific tab by tabId. Payload can then send subsequent steps to the popup tab.

solution_steps.title: Add step action: switch_tab with tabId
solution_steps.description: Payload can route subsequent steps to popup tab. Like existing 'switch_tab' but targets tabId instead of URL pattern.
solution_steps.pseudocode: {action: 'switch_tab', tabId: 1234} — routes all following steps to that tab until switch back
solution_steps.location: Extend existing switch_tab action in background.ts

solution_steps.title: Update payload schema
solution_steps.description: Runtime model gains 'focus_tab' and updated 'switch_tab' definitions.

minimum_extension_work.effort: 2–3 hours. Mostly socket.io listener + background worker chrome.tabs.query + one payload action. No CSP bypass needed.
minimum_extension_work.risk: Low. Follows existing patterns (list_tabs already exists in background). No new extension APIs or user prompts.

alternative_approaches.reason: chrome.debugger requires the user to grant permission per-popup, and popups don't typically have debugger access for security reasons.

alternative_approaches.approach: Inject content script into popup after window.open()
alternative_approaches.reason: Can inject, but popup may be cross-origin and CSP-hostile. Also, popup is transient — once user closes it, session is lost. Better to control it via background worker.

alternative_approaches.approach: Use MCP tool to drive popup via system automation (osascript, etc.)
alternative_approaches.reason: Defeats the purpose of browser automation. Also fragile across OS and browser versions.

account_chooser_default_strategy.title: Selecting mw@mike-wolf.com when multiple accounts shown
account_chooser_default_strategy.implementation: Payload step 'select account' uses fallbackSelectors cascade: [data-email] → [data-identifier] → text match → escalate.
account_chooser_default_strategy.google_accounts_page: Google's accounts.google.com shows accounts as list items with [data-email='...'] attributes. Clicking [data-email='mw@mike-wolf.com'] selects that account.
account_chooser_default_strategy.yeshid_pattern: YeshID login page shows account options as list items, each with data-email or text content.
account_chooser_default_strategy.current_implementation: PRE_CLICK_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT(email) in background.ts already handles this for in-tab account chooser. Works for surfaces 1 & 2.
account_chooser_default_strategy.note: For surface 3 (popup), the same PRE_CLICK_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT function needs to run inside the popup tab. Once 'switch_tab' is implemented, payload can call PRE_CLICK_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT in the popup context.
